Order on Board 02.03.2026
1.

The instant review petition has been filed for modification of order dated 23.06.2025 passed in
Wpc No. 2879 of 2020.
2.

Mr. Vaibhav Shukla, Advocate appearing for the review petitioner/ Power Grid Corporation Of India Ltd. would submit that due to inadvertence submission was made that the writ petition filed by the petitioner was not maintainable according to the provisions of Section 16(3) of Indian Telegraph Act, 1885(for short "Act, 1885").

entities.text: Power Grid Corporation Of India Ltd.
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
He would submit that actually the writ petitioner had remedy to approach Collector according to the provisions of Section 34 of Land Acquisition Act,
1894(for short "Act, 1894").
He would submit that modification requires in para 4 and para 7 of order passed in WPC No. 2879 of 2020 dated 23.06.2025.
3. Ms. Anuradha Jain, Dy. Government Advocate appearing for the State would support the contention made by Mr. Shukla.
4. On the other hand, Mr. Chatterjee would submit that writ petition was disposed of on submission made by review petitioner, therefore, review petition may be dismissed.
5. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the documents placed on record.

6. It appears that the land of the writ petitioner was acquired by the State for Power Grid Corporation Of India Ltd. and WPC No. 2879 of 2020 was filed claiming therein interest on amount of compensation.

entities.text: Power Grid Corporation Of India Ltd.
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Land oustee had remedy to approach Collector according to the provisions of Section 34 of Act, 1894, but due to mistake liberty was granted to approach the authority according to the provisions of Section 16(3) of the Act, 1885.
The mistake appears to be bonafide, and therefore, the prayer made by Mr. Vaibhav Shukla is hereby allowed.
In para 4 and para 7, instead of Section 16(3) of Indian Telegraph Act, 1885, Section 34 of Land Acquisition Act, 1894 shall be substituted.
7. This order shall be part of order passed in WPC No. 2879 of 2020.
8. It is informed that the writ petitioner has already preferred an appeal before the District Judge as per provisions of Telegraph Act, 1885.

The writ petitioner would be at liberty to withdraw said appeal and would be at liberty to prefer application/petition according to the provisions of Land Deputy General Manager Power Grid ... vs Ganesh Ram Yadav on 2 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/38406502/
2 Acquisition Act, 1894.
9.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: If the petitioner prefers an application according to the provisions of Act, 1884 before the Collector.
It is expected that said authority shall decide it expeditiously.
10. This MCC has been preferred for extension of time.

11. As the liberty has already granted to the writ petitioner to withdraw appeal preferred by him pending before the District Judge, there is no need to pass any order for extension of time to decide the pending appeal.
Accordingly, instant MCC is disposed of.
